_(This property has no documentation)_

### [bool](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_bool.html)
 **full\_load\_mode\_enabled** = false[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#bool-full_load_mode_enabled-false "Permanent link")

If enabled, data streaming will be turned off, and all voxel data will be loaded from the [stream](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#i_stream)
 into memory.

This removes several constraints, such as being able to edit anywhere and allowing distant normalmaps to include edited regions. This comes at the expense of more memory usage. However, only edited regions use memory, so in practice it can be good enough.

### [bool](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_bool.html)
 **generate\_collisions** = true[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#bool-generate_collisions-true "Permanent link")

If enabled, chunked colliders will be generated from meshes.

### [int](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_int.html)
 **lod\_count** = 4[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#int-lod_count-4 "Permanent link")

How many LOD levels to use. This should be tuned alongside [lod\_distance](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#i_lod_distance)
: if you want to see very far, you need more LOD levels. This allows blocks to become larger the further away they are, to keep their numbers to an acceptable amount. In contrast, too few LOD levels means regions far away will have to use too many small blocks, which can affect performance.

### [float](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_float.html)
 **lod\_distance** = 48.0[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#float-lod_distance-480 "Permanent link")

How far LOD 0 extends from the viewer. Each parent LOD will extend twice as far as their children LOD levels. When [full\_load\_mode\_enabled](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#i_full_load_mode_enabled)
 is disabled, this also defines how far edits are allowed.

For further control of LODs beyond 0, see [secondary\_lod\_distance](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#i_secondary_lod_distance)
.

### [float](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_float.html)
 **lod\_fade\_duration** = 0.0[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#float-lod_fade_duration-00 "Permanent link")

When set greater than 0, enables LOD fading. When mesh blocks get split/merged as level of detail changes, they will fade to make the transition less noticeable (or at least more pleasant). This feature requires to use a specific shader, check the online documentation or examples for more information.

### [Material](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_material.html)
 **material**[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#material-material "Permanent link")

Material used for the surface of the volume. The main usage of this node is with smooth voxels, which means if you want more than one "material" on the ground, you need to use splatmapping techniques with a shader. In addition, many features require shaders to work properly. Check the online documentation or examples for more information.

Note: if you use a [ShaderMaterial](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_shadermaterial.html)
, it will be instanced on every chunk in order to support per-chunk/LOD features, so dynamic changes done to parameters will not apply. You can use [global uniforms](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/shaders/shader_reference/shading_language.html#global-uniforms)
 to workaround this limitation.

### [int](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_int.html)
 **mesh\_block\_size** = 16[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#int-mesh_block_size-16 "Permanent link")

Sets how many voxels across meshes of the terrain span.

Voxel chunks are stored in cubic chunks of 16x16x16 voxels, and by default meshes of the terrain match that size. But you can set this to 32 so meshes will span 2x2x2 voxel chunks. This is a performance tradeoff. Higher mesh size may speed up rendering, at the cost of slower mesh updates.

Values other than 16 and 32 are not supported.

Note: this setting also affects [VoxelInstancer](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelInstancer/)
 chunks.

### [int](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_int.html)
 **normalmap\_begin\_lod\_index** = 2[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#int-normalmap_begin_lod_index-2 "Permanent link")

From which LOD index normalmaps will be generated. There won't be normalmaps below this index.

### [bool](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_bool.html)
 **normalmap\_enabled** = false[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#bool-normalmap_enabled-false "Permanent link")

Enables generation of distant normalmaps. This is a feature used with smooth terrain only (SDF). It is an expensive feature but allows to bring a lot more detail to distant ground.

This feature requires to use a specific shader, check the online documentation or examples for more information.

### [int](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_int.html)
 **normalmap\_max\_deviation\_degrees** = 60[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#int-normalmap_max_deviation_degrees-60 "Permanent link")

_(This property has no documentation)_

### [bool](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_bool.html)
 **normalmap\_octahedral\_encoding\_enabled** = false[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#bool-normalmap_octahedral_encoding_enabled-false "Permanent link")

Enables octahedral compression of normalmaps, which reduces memory usage caused by distant normalmaps by about 33%, with some impact on visual quality. Your shader may be modified accordingly to decode them.

### [int](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_int.html)
 **normalmap\_tile\_resolution\_max** = 8[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#int-normalmap_tile_resolution_max-8 "Permanent link")

Maximum resolution of tiles in distant normalmaps.

### [int](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_int.html)
 **normalmap\_tile\_resolution\_min** = 4[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#int-normalmap_tile_resolution_min-4 "Permanent link")

Minimum resolution of tiles in distant normalmaps.

This is the resolution at which normalmaps will begin with, at the LOD level defined in [normalmap\_begin\_lod\_index](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#i_normalmap_begin_lod_index)
. Resolutions will double at each LOD level, until they reach [normalmap\_tile\_resolution\_max](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#i_normalmap_tile_resolution_max)
.

### [bool](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_bool.html)
 **normalmap\_use\_gpu** = false[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#bool-normalmap_use_gpu-false "Permanent link")

Enables GPU detail normalmaps generation, which can speed it up. This is only valid for generators that support it. Vulkan is required.

### [float](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_float.html)
 **secondary\_lod\_distance** = 48.0[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#float-secondary_lod_distance-480 "Permanent link")

Controls the size of each LOD above LOD 0, in voxels relative to those LODs (voxels of LOD N are twice as big than LOD N-1). Higher values allow to see further away before detail are decimated, but is more expensive.

Note that it will not necessarily be respected accurately, and will rather be used as a target minimum distance.

This is only used when [streaming\_system](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#i_streaming_system)
 is set to [STREAMING\_SYSTEM\_CLIPBOX](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#i_STREAMING_SYSTEM_CLIPBOX)
. In other cases, [lod\_distance](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#i_lod_distance)
 is used.

To control LOD 0, see [lod\_distance](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#i_lod_distance)
.

### [StreamingSystem](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#enumerations)
 **streaming\_system** = STREAMING\_SYSTEM\_LEGACY\_OCTREE (0)[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#streamingsystem-streaming_system-streaming_system_legacy_octree-0 "Permanent link")

Selects the underlying algorithm used to determine when to load and unload chunks around viewers as they move around.

### [bool](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_bool.html)
 **threaded\_update\_enabled** = false[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#bool-threaded_update_enabled-false "Permanent link")

When enabled, this node will run a large part of its update cycle in a separate thread. Otherwise, it will run on the main thread.

### [bool](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_bool.html)
 **use\_gpu\_generation** = false[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#bool-use_gpu_generation-false "Permanent link")

Enables GPU block generation, which can speed it up. This is only valid for generators that support it. Vulkan is required.

### [int](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_int.html)
 **view\_distance** = 512[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#int-view_distance-512 "Permanent link")

Maximum distance viewers can have. If a viewer has a larger distance, it will be clamped. Note that this is only a hint and not an exact boundary. Terrain may load within that distance, but can continue beyond it, rounding up to block size of the biggest LOD.

If your terrain size is finite (like an island or planet) and you want to keep it in view, you may want to set this value to a very large number. This is mainly useful for infinite terrains where a cap is desired.

### [AABB](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_aabb.html)
 **voxel\_bounds** = AABB(-536870900, -536870900, -536870900, 1073741800, 1073741800, 1073741800)[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#aabb-voxel_bounds-aabb-536870900-536870900-536870900-1073741800-1073741800-1073741800 "Permanent link")

Bounds within which volume data can exist (loaded or not), in voxels. By default, it is pseudo-infinite. If you make a planet, island or some sort of arena, you may want to choose a finite size.

Note, because this volume uses chunks with LOD, these bounds will snap to the closest chunk boundary.

### [Array](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_array.html)
 **debug\_get\_octrees\_detailed**( )[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#array-debug_get_octrees_detailed "Permanent link")

Gets debug information about the grid of octrees used to stream the terrain at multiple levels of detail.

The returned array contains alternating [Vector3i](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_vector3i.html)
 and [Array](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_array.html)
 values, where each pair corresponds to one octree at a specific position:

    [\
        Vector3i,\
        Array,\
        Vector3i,\
        Array,\
        ...\
    ]
    

The array after positions contains info about one octree:

    [\
        int (node state),\
        null or Array (children info)\
    ]
    

When children info is not null, it contains 8 arrays structured the same way, and may be recursively traversed to obtain the state of every node of the octree.

        "time_detect_required_blocks": int,

        "time_process_update_responses": int,

### [bool](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_bool.html)
 **is\_area\_meshed**( [AABB](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_aabb.html)
 area\_in\_voxels, [int](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_int.html)
 lod\_index )[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#bool-is_area_meshed-aabb-area_in_voxels-int-lod_index "Permanent link")

Returns true if the area has been processed by meshing. It does not mean the area actually contains a mesh.

Returns false if the area has not been processed by meshing (therefore it is unknown whethere there should be a mesh here or not).

When streaming terrain, this can be used to determine if an area has fully "loaded", in case the game relies meshes or mesh colliders.

### [VoxelSaveCompletionTracker](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelSaveCompletionTracker/)
 **save\_modified\_blocks**( )[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelLodTerrain/#voxelsavecompletiontracker-save_modified_blocks "Permanent link")

Requests saving of all modified voxels. Saving is asynchronous and will complete some time in the future. If the game quits, the engine will ensure saving tasks get completed before the application shuts down.

Use the returned tracker object to know when saving has completed. However, saves occurring after calling this method won't be tracked by this object.

Note that blocks getting unloaded as the viewer moves around can also trigger saving tasks, independently from this function.

# VoxelBuffer - Voxel Tools documentation

*   [](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/)
    
*   Scripting API
*   VoxelBuffer

* * *

VoxelBuffer[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#voxelbuffer "Permanent link")

===========================================================================================================

Inherits: [RefCounted](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_refcounted.html)

3D grid storing voxel data.

Description:[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#description "Permanent link")

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This contains dense voxels data storage (every single cell holds data, there is no sparse optimization of space). Works like a normal 3D grid containing a voxel value in each cell. Organized in channels of configurable bit depth. Values can be interpreted either as unsigned integers, fixed-point or floats. See [Depth](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#enumerations)
 for more information.

Arbitrary metadata can also be stored, either for the whole buffer, or per-voxel, at higher cost. This metadata can get saved and loaded along voxels, however you must make sure the data is serializable (i.e it should not contain nodes or arbitrary objects).

Enumerations:[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#enumerations "Permanent link")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

enum **ChannelId**:

*   **CHANNEL\_TYPE** = **0** --- Channel used to store voxel types. Used by [VoxelMesherBlocky](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelMesherBlocky/)
    .
*   **CHANNEL\_SDF** = **1** --- Channel used to store SDF data (signed distance field). Used by [VoxelMesherTransvoxel](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelMesherTransvoxel/)
     and other smooth meshers. Values should preferably be accessed as floats. Negative values are below the isosurface (inside matter), and positive values are above the surface (outside matter).
*   **CHANNEL\_COLOR** = **2** --- Channel used to store color data. Used by [VoxelMesherCubes](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelMesherCubes/)
    .
*   **CHANNEL\_INDICES** = **3** --- Channel used to store material indices. Used with smooth voxels.
*   **CHANNEL\_WEIGHTS** = **4** --- Channel used to store material weights, when more than one index can be stored per voxel. Used with smooth voxels.
*   **CHANNEL\_DATA5** = **5** --- Free channel. Not used by the engine yet.
*   **CHANNEL\_DATA6** = **6** --- Free channel. Not used by the engine yet.
*   **CHANNEL\_DATA7** = **7** --- Free channel. Not used by the engine yet.
*   **MAX\_CHANNELS** = **8** --- Maximum number of channels a [VoxelBuffer](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/)
     can have.

enum **ChannelMask**:

*   **CHANNEL\_TYPE\_BIT** = **1** --- Bitmask with one bit set at the position corresponding to [CHANNEL\_TYPE](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#i_CHANNEL_TYPE)
    .
*   **CHANNEL\_SDF\_BIT** = **2** --- Bitmask with one bit set at the position corresponding to [CHANNEL\_SDF](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#i_CHANNEL_SDF)
    .
*   **CHANNEL\_COLOR\_BIT** = **4** --- Bitmask with one bit set at the position corresponding to [CHANNEL\_COLOR](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#i_CHANNEL_COLOR)
    .
*   **CHANNEL\_INDICES\_BIT** = **8** --- Bitmask with one bit set at the position corresponding to [CHANNEL\_INDICES](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#i_CHANNEL_INDICES)
    .
*   **CHANNEL\_WEIGHTS\_BIT** = **16** --- Bitmask with one bit set at the position corresponding to [CHANNEL\_WEIGHTS](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#i_CHANNEL_WEIGHTS)
    .
*   **CHANNEL\_DATA5\_BIT** = **32** --- Bitmask with one bit set at the position corresponding to [CHANNEL\_DATA5](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#i_CHANNEL_DATA5)
    .
*   **CHANNEL\_DATA6\_BIT** = **64** --- Bitmask with one bit set at the position corresponding to [CHANNEL\_DATA6](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#i_CHANNEL_DATA6)
    .
*   **CHANNEL\_DATA7\_BIT** = **128** --- Bitmask with one bit set at the position corresponding to [CHANNEL\_DATA7](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#i_CHANNEL_DATA7)
    .
*   **ALL\_CHANNELS\_MASK** = **255** --- Bitmask with all channel bits set.

enum **Depth**:

*   **DEPTH\_8\_BIT** = **0** --- Voxels will be stored with 8 bits. Raw values will range from 0 to 255. Float values can take 255 values distributed from -10.0 to 10.0. Values outside the range will be clamped.
*   **DEPTH\_16\_BIT** = **1** --- Voxels will be stored with 16 bits. Raw values will range from 0 to 65,535. Float values can take 65,535 values distributed from -500.0 to 500.0. Values outside the range will be clamped.
*   **DEPTH\_32\_BIT** = **2** --- Voxels will be stored with 32 bits. Raw values will range from 0 to 4,294,967,295, and float values will use regular IEEE 754 representation (`float`).
*   **DEPTH\_64\_BIT** = **3** --- Voxels will be stored with 64 bits. Raw values will range from 0 to 18,446,744,073,709,551,615, and float values will use regular IEEE 754 representation (`double`).
*   **DEPTH\_COUNT** = **4** --- How many depth configuration there are.

enum **Compression**:

*   **COMPRESSION\_NONE** = **0** --- The channel is not compressed. Every value is stored individually inside an array in memory.
*   **COMPRESSION\_UNIFORM** = **1** --- All voxels of the channel have the same value, so they are stored as one single value, to save space.
*   **COMPRESSION\_COUNT** = **2** --- How many compression modes there are.

enum **Allocator**:

*   **ALLOCATOR\_DEFAULT** = **0** --- Uses Godot's default memory allocator (at time of writing, it is `malloc`). Preferred for occasional buffers with uncommon size, or very large size.
*   **ALLOCATOR\_POOL** = **1** --- Uses a pool allocator. Can be faster than the default allocator buffers are created very frequently with similar size. This memory will remain allocated after use, under the assumption that other buffers will need it soon after. Does not support very large buffers (greater than 2 megabytes)
*   **ALLOCATOR\_COUNT** = **2**

Constants:[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#constants "Permanent link")

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

*   **MAX\_SIZE** = **65535** --- Maximum size a buffer can have when serialized. Buffers that contain uniform-compressed voxels can reach it, but in practice, the limit is much lower and depends on available memory.

Method Descriptions[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#method-descriptions "Permanent link")

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### [void](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#)
 **clear**( )[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#void-clear "Permanent link")

Erases all contents of the buffer and resets its size to zero. Channel depths and default values are preserved.

### [void](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#)
 **clear\_voxel\_metadata**( )[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#void-clear_voxel_metadata "Permanent link")

Erases all per-voxel metadata.

### [void](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#)
 **clear\_voxel\_metadata\_in\_area**( [Vector3i](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_vector3i.html)
 min\_pos, [Vector3i](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_vector3i.html)
 max\_pos )[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#void-clear_voxel_metadata_in_area-vector3i-min_pos-vector3i-max_pos "Permanent link")

Erases per-voxel metadata within the specified area.

### [void](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#)
 **compress\_uniform\_channels**( )[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#void-compress_uniform_channels "Permanent link")

Finds channels that have the same value in all their voxels, and reduces memory usage by storing only one value instead. This is effective for example when large parts of the terrain are filled with air.

### [void](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#)
 **copy\_channel\_from**( [VoxelBuffer](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/)
 other, [int](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_int.html)
 channel )[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#void-copy_channel_from-voxelbuffer-other-int-channel "Permanent link")

Copies all values from the channel of another [VoxelBuffer](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/)
 into the same channel for the current buffer. The depth formats must match.

### [void](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#)
 **copy\_channel\_from\_area**( [VoxelBuffer](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/)
 other, [Vector3i](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_vector3i.html)
 src\_min, [Vector3i](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_vector3i.html)
 src\_max, [Vector3i](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_vector3i.html)
 dst\_min, [int](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_int.html)
 channel )[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#void-copy_channel_from_area-voxelbuffer-other-vector3i-src_min-vector3i-src_max-vector3i-dst_min-int-channel "Permanent link")

Copies values from a channel's sub-region of another [VoxelBuffer](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/)
 into the same channel for the current buffer, at a specific location. The depth formats must match.

If corners of the area represent a negative-size area, they will be sorted back.

If coordinates are entirely or partially out of bounds, they will be clipped automatically.

Copying across the same buffer to overlapping areas is not supported. You may use an intermediary buffer in this case.

### [void](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#)
 **copy\_voxel\_metadata\_in\_area**( [VoxelBuffer](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/)
 src\_buffer, [Vector3i](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_vector3i.html)
 src\_min\_pos, [Vector3i](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_vector3i.html)
 src\_max\_pos, [Vector3i](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_vector3i.html)
 dst\_min\_pos )[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#void-copy_voxel_metadata_in_area-voxelbuffer-src_buffer-vector3i-src_min_pos-vector3i-src_max_pos-vector3i-dst_min_pos "Permanent link")

Copies per-voxel metadata from a sub-region of another [VoxelBuffer](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/)
 into the the current buffer, at a specific location. Values will be a shallow copy.

If corners of the area represent a negative-size area, they will be sorted back.

If coordinates are entirely or partially out of bounds, they will be clipped automatically.

Copying across the same buffer to overlapping areas is not supported. You may use an intermediary buffer in this case.

### [ImageTexture3D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_imagetexture3d.html)
 **create\_3d\_texture\_from\_sdf\_zxy**( [Format](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_image.html#enum-image-format)
 output\_format )[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#imagetexture3d-create_3d_texture_from_sdf_zxy-format-output_format "Permanent link")

Creates a 3D texture from the SDF channel.

If `output_format` is a 8-bit pixel format, the texture will contain normalized signed distances, where 0.5 is the isolevel, 0 is the furthest away under surface, and 1 is the furthest away above surface.

Only 16-bit SDF channel is supported.

Only [Image.FORMAT\_R8](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_image.html#class-image-constant-FORMAT-R8)
 and [Image.FORMAT\_L8](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_image.html#class-image-constant-FORMAT-L8)
 output formats are suported.

Note: when sampling this texture in a shader, you need to swizzle 3D coordinates with `.yxz`. This is how voxels are internally stored, and this function does not change this convention.

### [Image\[\]](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_image[].html)
 **debug\_print\_sdf\_y\_slices**( [float](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_float.html)
 scale=1.0 )[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#image-debug_print_sdf_y_slices-float-scale10 "Permanent link")

Renders the contents of the SDF channel into images where blue gradients are negative values (below surface) and yellow gradients are positive (above surface). Each image corresponds to an XZ slice of the buffer.

The `scale` parameter can be used to change contrast of images by scaling the SDF.

Rotates voxel values by 90 degrees along the specified axis. 1 turn is 90 degrees, 2 turns is 180 degrees, 3 turns is 270 degrees (or -90), 4 turns does nothing. Negative turns go in the other direction. This may also rotate the size of the buffer, if it isn't cubic.

If this [VoxelBuffer](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/)
 is saved, this metadata will also be saved along voxels, so make sure the data supports serialization (i.e you can't put nodes or arbitrary objects in it).

### [void](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#)
 **set\_voxel\_metadata**( [Vector3i](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_vector3i.html)
 pos, [Variant](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_variant.html)
 value )[¶](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/#void-set_voxel_metadata-vector3i-pos-variant-value "Permanent link")

Attaches arbitrary data on a specific voxel. Old data is replaced. Passing `null` will erase metadata.

If this [VoxelBuffer](https://voxel-tools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/VoxelBuffer/)
 is saved, this metadata will also be saved along voxels, so make sure the data supports serialization (i.e you can't put nodes or arbitrary objects in it).
